# #279 correctness review

## A. Verdict

**BLOCK** at `30040fc8653d05fea322ed48d63ee8e5a08f7ee1`, base `9ffc5729843e9e0aac6825165a7de31b4d30d6ce`.

Two executable normal-use recovery defects strand the work this PR promises to carry. These are not optional hardening or per-seat security isolation. No earlier reviewer output or GitHub review was recorded when this review began; the author's "round 2" was the no-backfill revision.

## B. Summary

The same-process/same-launch native-boundary admission and the store's transactional boundary check are sound at the reviewed head. The intent gate correctly prevents historical backfill. Carry recovery nevertheless loses its discovery inputs during a partial index update, and it cannot follow two native boundaries whose first asynchronous carry has not finished.

## C. Requested checks

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Same-process, same non-null spawn ID, native boundary | Static trace and exact-head guard tests pass. Registration verifies predecessor process identity before admitting Start::New. Ordinary revive/restart does not itself create a new carry. |
| Store guard and HTTP reachability | One production caller of carry_mail_committed, in carry.rs; no HTTP route. BEGIN IMMEDIATE verifies the seats rows and moves mail/events in the same transaction. |
| Historical boundary without intent | Exact-head test passes; removing the intent gate makes that test fail. |
| Request delivering at clear, refused project, stamps | Existing carry suite passes in the local full Rust gate. Refused-project and delivering semantics match the stated contract in those tests. |
| Old answer between holdings read/update and mail transaction | Reviewer probe passes: no requeue and no successor copy. |
| F193 drains racing carry | Reviewer probe passes: one delivery copy. |
| Crash during index end/start | **R279-001: fails.** |
| Two clear boundaries before the first async carry | **R279-002: fails.** |
| Runtime/std-Mutex and git placement | Carry uses async locks and Tokio sleep. Short std-Mutex guards do not cross awaits; governance git work runs in spawn_blocking, not in the registration caller's locked task. |
| Cost | No new steady-state timer/poll/launch: 0 added idle launches/s. Per clear: intent, one existing governance-writer invocation per held project, indexed writes/mail transaction and drain; up to 20 settle attempts. Existing writer documents seven git launches per write plus validation/build per changed document. Boot redo is one roster scan plus eligible spine reads, once. No live deployment or before/after fleet change was made. |

## D. Findings

| ID | Severity | Location | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| R279-001 | HIGH | crates/daemon/src/community/directory.rs:2378-2395; crates/daemon/src/carry.rs:190-203 | Separately committed index ends erase the only discovery input before successor starts are persisted. |
| R279-002 | HIGH | crates/daemon/src/carry.rs:67-71, 164-171, 380-387; crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:1756-1758 | A second clear tombstones the intermediate successor, so the pending first carry is skipped permanently. |

## E. Executable reproductions

**R279-001:** `reviewer_carry_recovers_crash_between_index_end_and_start` records the real intent, holds EventBus's publication boundary, and runs the real carry_project. After end_assignments has committed, it aborts the caller while the successor's start is still waiting for admission. It releases the boundary and invokes boot redo. The governance document contains the successor's holding, but neither seat has an open index row. Carry discovers no project or scope, records completion, and the request remains `(Delivered, Some("pij-holder"))`, not the expected successor. This is a real interruption of the implementation, not manually deleting rows. A daemon interruption has the same persisted gap. Make ends and starts atomic, or retain sufficient durable discovery to repair an incomplete index before recording the carry done.

**R279-002:** `reviewer_carry_reaches_latest_successor_after_two_clear_boundaries` establishes two same-launch native-boundary pairs, A -> B -> C, before executing the scheduled carries. The first carry rejects B because B is now retired; it records no intent. The second finds no holdings on B. Boot skips A because its immediate successor B is not live. The request remains `(Delivered, Some("pij-holder"))`, not the expected latest successor. Two clears during asynchronous carry, or while another carry holds the global async gate, can therefore strand holdings, requests and FYIs. Preserve and finish work across proven boundary chains without relaxing same-process/same-launch provenance or enabling historical backfill.

## F. Coverage and limits

The review was read-only over the 13-file exact-head diff and adjacent registration, governance-index, event publication, request and delivery paths. Reviewer tests were added only to a disposable git-archive source copy; its product files matched the assigned head before the requested mutation.

The delegated C33-scoped static security review found no authorization vulnerability:

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | None found within the C33 scope | - |

No live Copilot clear was performed; assembled live proof remains separate from these real-SQLite/git integration receipts. Two additional static observations are **C34 follow-ups**, not blockers here: completion/intent records keyed only by predecessor ID may suppress a later carry after ID reuse; a prevalidated old reply stamped after the mail transaction may leave queued-and-answered work that a drain redundantly delivers. The passing old-answer probe specifically covers the requested before-mail timing, not that later window.

## G. Commands and evidence

All cargo work used the canonical shared target, shared-build's lock, niceness 19 and four jobs. Commands below are the exact recipe argv; PIJ_SHARED_TARGET was set to the canonical target. Mutation/probe commands ran in the isolated exact-head copy.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| just pr-freeze 279 | PASS, including final recheck: assigned head still FINAL and checkout clean. |
| harness boot --json | Exit 0 advisory, ready=false: local vitest/TS dependencies absent. Not a readiness pass. |
| just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --test directory_http carry --then test --locked -p pij-daemon --test directory_http a_boundary_without_a_recorded_intent_is_never_redone | Exit 0: 5 selected tests plus the historical-intent test pass. |
| harness checks --json | Exit 1: missing dependency/tooling stages and incompatible ambient Biome. Rust fmt/clippy/workspace tests, route inventory, native contracts/SDK, skill structure and smoke pass. Exact-head CI is green; no dependency symlink or installation was made. |
| just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --test directory_http reviewer_ | Exit 101: 3 pass, 2 fail. The two failing new probes are R279-001 and R279-002; old-answer and racing-drain probes pass, as does one pre-existing reviewer replay test selected by the filter. |
| just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --test directory_http a_boundary_without_a_recorded_intent_is_never_redone (intent gate disabled only in isolated copy) | Exit 101: one test executed; expected assertion left `(0,1)`, right `(1,0)`. Mutation caught. |
| just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --test directory_http a_boundary_without_a_recorded_intent_is_never_redone (untouched assigned checkout after mutation) | Exit 0: one test passes; shared artifacts rebuilt from the correct source after the mutant. |

Retained receipts in the standing governance worktree, relative to that worktree:

- `.harness/records/retro/2026-11-20/review-279-carry-probes.log`
- `.harness/records/retro/2026-11-20/review-279-carry-regressions.diff`
- `.harness/records/retro/2026-11-20/review-279-no-intent-mutant.log`
- `.harness/records/retro/2026-11-20/review-279-restored-guard.log`

The log receipts are scrubbed of machine home paths; the patch has portable repository-relative labels. Original source was never edited.

## H. Handover and harness gift

Fix only the two proven carry failures, using the retained executable test patch as the regression harness. The standing governance retrospective is `.harness/records/retro/2026-11-20/001-review-279-carry.md`. Its magic wand is fault injection at each independent committed index mutation, not only after the complete carry_project call. The PM owns landing these fixtures and any C34 follow-up dispositions; the reviewer does not edit implementation or push.
